english: Let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{x^{n}\log_{e}x+\sqrt{x}-1}{x^{n}+1}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1+h)\,f(1-h)}{h^{2}}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{x^{n}\log_{e}x+\sqrt{x}-1}{x^{n}+1}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1+h)\,f(1-h)}{h^{2}}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The two pieces swap but the product is the same, so the limit is $-\dfrac12=-0.5$
solution_full: Finding $f$. For $x>1$, divide numerator and denominator by $x^{n}$: $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim\dfrac{\ln x+(\sqrt{x}-1)x^{-n}}{1+x^{-n}}=\ln x$. For $0<x<1$, $x^{n}\to0$, so $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$. At $x=1$, $f(1)=\dfrac{0+0}{1+1}=0$.
So $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$ on $(0,1)$, $f(1)=0$, $f(x)=\ln x$ on $(1,\infty)$: a function given by different formulas on the two sides of $1$.

Right side, $0<h<1$: $1+h>1$ and $1-h<1$, so $\dfrac{f(1+h)f(1-h)}{h^{2}}=\dfrac{\ln(1+h)}{h}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{1-h}-1}{h}$. Here $\dfrac{\ln(1+h)}{h}\to1$ and $\dfrac{\sqrt{1-h}-1}{h}=\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1-h}+1}\to-\dfrac{1}{2}$; the product tends to $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Left side, $-1<h<0$: now $1+h<1$ and $1-h>1$, so the quotient is $\dfrac{\sqrt{1+h}-1}{h}\cdot\dfrac{\ln(1-h)}{h}$. Here $\dfrac{\sqrt{1+h}-1}{h}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+h}+1}\to\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\ln(1-h)}{h}\to-1$; the product tends to $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.
The one-sided limits agree although $f$ itself has different one-sided slopes at $1$ ($1$ and $\dfrac12$). Hence the limit is $-\dfrac{1}{2}=-0.50$.
originality_note: New: a function produced by the x^n limit has different formulas on the two sides of 1, and the product f(1+h)f(1-h) always takes one factor from each side, so the two one-sided limits coincide although f has a corner (way 2 and way 4). Closest known: f(x) = lim (x^{2n} g(x) + h(x))/(x^{2n} + 1) with continuity checks at |x| = 1. Different because: the limit asked is two-sided only because the branches swap, which the student must notice.
blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving non uniformly defined functions

concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving non unifor: The quotient takes ln on one side of 1 and sqrt(x) - 1 on the other; both one-sided limits are evaluated separately and agree at -1/2.
concept_use.Functions defined by a limit, e.g. lim o: f is first obtained from the limit in n: ln x for x > 1, sqrt(x) - 1 for 0 < x < 1, 0 at x = 1.

key_step: Writing f piecewise from the n-limit and noticing that f(1+h)f(1-h) uses one branch of each kind on both sides.
